column2: follow-up question (asked when this keyPoint is uncertain; must not contain the answer)
Why should a government have to return to the voters at fixed intervals, and what power does a vote give you?
Which offices do voters choose themselves in India and which are chosen by elected representatives instead?
In a constituency with three candidates who get 40, 35 and 25 per cent of the votes, who wins under India's system for the Lok Sabha, and why?
How does voting for a party rather than a person change how many seats each party gets, and which Indian offices are filled this way?
Which law deals with preparing voter lists and drawing constituencies, and which with how candidates are nominated and campaigns and polls are run?
What kinds of promises or appeals are illegal during an election campaign in India?
If one district's population doubles while another's stays the same, what unfairness arises in representation unless boundaries change?
What does delimitation decide and which body does it, and under which Article?
Which constitutional body runs all elections in India, when was it set up and why is it independent of the government?
List three jobs the Election Commission does before a single vote is cast, and what the exercise to update and verify voter lists is for.
Under what conditions would an election be held yet lose its democratic value?
What can the ECI do for a voter who is 88 years old or has a disability, and how can a citizen report a code-of-conduct violation quickly?
Where do most voters first learn about candidates and their plans, and what do parties do that helps them choose?
Why does India have so many political parties, and how does the ECI sort them into national, state and unrecognised ones?
What exactly counts as defection for a legislator who won on a party's ticket?
Why was a law passed to stop legislators changing sides, and what happens to a member who goes against the party's instructions?
When did alliance politics begin in India, and which alliance formed the first coalition government at the centre?
What threatens fairness in a huge election, and which safeguards, from machines to paper trails, does the ECI use?
